_comment: TENANT FACTS. This is the only file in the toolkit permitted to contain a
domain name, a server name, or an organisation's internal vocabulary.
Everything else reads from here. If a tenant name appears in a .ps1 file,
that is a bug -- Test-Toolkit checks for it.
Engineer preferences (paths, browser profiles) live in Settings.json, not
here. This file is the same on every machine at a tenant; that one is not.
Servers is the on-premises Exchange server list. Site and Role are DECLARED,
never derived from the name: Role is Mailbox or Edge, and Site is any
label you like -- it only has to be the SAME for servers that must not
reboot at the same time. A bare list of names still loads, but those
servers cannot be rebooted until they have a Site and a Role.
ExcludedServers are shown greyed with the reason, never ticked.
ConnectionServers (optional): the Mailbox servers a tool may open its
remote Exchange shell through, used VERBATIM when present. Leave it out and
the tool derives the list from Servers. Set it to reproduce exactly the
connection behaviour of a script that named its connection servers itself.
Where the Feature Request tool sends requests. The operator never sees
this address -- it goes on BCC -- but it is not a secret: it is in a
config file anyone can open. It lives here rather than in the script
because Test-Toolkit rejects a mail domain written into a .ps1.
Servers the Server Health tool checks: disk, patch level, pending
updates, reboot state. A WIDER list than OnPremExchange.Servers, which
means 'servers the Exchange tools may run cmdlets against' -- this one
includes domain controllers, file servers and anything else worth
watching.
Exchange true/false is a HINT, not a gate. The check reports Exchange
wherever it finds it; the flag only decides whether ABSENCE is a
finding. Notes is free text and is shown nowhere -- it is for whoever
opens this file next.
Absent means off: no block, no servers, and the tool says so rather
than reporting a clean estate of nothing. Edit it in Tenant Manager.
